key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameter control can help produce protective coatings for carbon-steel components exposed to corrosion and sliding wear.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, coating porosity, and lamellar microstructure.
Test long-term corrosion and sliding wear under different humidity conditions using Si3N4 balls.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficients and wear rates as humidity increases.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance values or test ranges, and the humidity-dependent wear findings may depend on the Si3N4 counterface.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
